deploymentRepo.note: The deployment platform uses a TWO-repository model: the application repo (source) and a separate deployment repo (GitOps manifests). This block exists so our skills recognize the second repo, NOT so they create it.
deploymentRepo.syncedBy: Argo CD — it ALWAYS syncs from this repository, never from the application repo
deploymentRepo.createdBy: The deployment platform at onboarding. Never by us.
deploymentRepo.visibility: the deployment repo is accessible only to the SRE/platform team. `gh` returns 404 to us, and that means no access as often as absence — it is NOT evidence the repo is missing. Never infer onboarding state from it; confirm with the platform team or SRE.
ourRules: Never create it — not with create-github-repo, not with gh repo create, not by hand.
Never push to it. Manifest changes go through the platform team or a reviewed PR by whoever owns deployments — not through push-to-github.
Never treat a 404 from gh as absence — the repo is SRE/platform-only and invisible to us; confirm with the platform team or SRE.
Never treat its absence as a problem. A project that has not been onboarded correctly has no deployment repo.
Never point create-github-repo at a deployment-* name; if the user asks for one, explain that onboarding creates it and stop.
If it does exist, Kubernetes manifest changes belong THERE, not in the application repo — a manifest appearing in the app repo is worth questioning.
deploymentRepo.webhooks: Push webhooks on both repos point at https://webhooks.acme.example/webhook/github. For onboarded apps the platform's webhooks and CI pipeline own CI/CD; GitHub Actions are not required. Ask the platform team to repair missing webhooks rather than re-onboarding.
